correctness.rationale: Send L to y=0 and Q to [0:1:0], and normalize the four ordered directions to 0,∞,1,t. Each conic's polar of Q contains its two distinct contact points, hence is L, and Q is off the conic; the equation is uniquely y²+B_i before the common y-rescaling. Each adjacent binary difference has a double root in its contact direction: the tangent line has order two along either branch, so multiplicity four forces the square. Adding the four differences gives the unique coefficient proportions ((t−1),t(1−t),−t,1); scaling y over C and imposing the point incidences gives the four frozen quadratics. Their binary factors are distinct for t≠0,1, giving smooth conics. The four square differences give the A₇ contacts, and no third conic contains any assigned contact. The opposite differences have two distinct roots each (discriminants nonzero and z=0 not a root); their roots do not hit the binary roots of those conics. Thus projection to [x:z] is unramified on y≠0 there, and a simple difference root lifts to two transverse intersections. Any triple would contain an adjacent pair, so this accounts for precisely eight nodes and four A₇ points. The uploaded verifier was read, not executed; an independent symbolic expansion established the cubic identity in Z[t,x,y,z]. The −2xy² coefficient of C ensures it survives all parameter specializations. Dimca–Sernesi gives mdr≥(5/8)·8−2=3, so mdr=3; τ=36 and the nearly-free criterion at d=8,r=3 gives exponents (3,5). The ordered contact quadruple recovers t, proving uniqueness for order-preserving projective equivalence only. The bibliographic caveat below concerns a prior example's misprinted equation, not the frozen normal form or its proof.
